extra.message: User input from request.GET['host'] is concatenated directly into a shell command passed to os.system(). An attacker can inject arbitrary OS commands using shell metacharacters (e.g., '; rm -rf /').

User-controlled data from request.body or request.GET['blob'] is deserialized with pickle.loads(), enabling arbitrary code execution. An attacker can craft a pickle payload that executes any Python code on the server.

User input from request.GET['fragment'] is interpolated into a Jinja2 Template string and rendered without sandboxing. This enables Server-Side Template Injection, allowing arbitrary code execution via Jinja2 constructs like {{ ''.__class__.__mro__[1].__subclasses__() }}.

User input from request.GET['ref'] is used directly in a path construction (BASE_EXPORT_DIR / f'{ref}.json') without sanitization. An attacker can use '../' sequences to write files to arbitrary locations on the filesystem. Additionally, the endpoint writes sensitive data (SSN, credit card numbers) to the file.

cwe: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

extra.message: User input from request.GET['name'] is used directly in a path construction (BASE_EXPORT_DIR / name) without sanitization, and request.body is written to that path. An attacker can use '../' sequences to write arbitrary content to arbitrary filesystem locations, potentially overwriting critical files.

cwe: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

extra.message: The acct_identity_ping_343 endpoint has no _wrk_gate() authentication check and no @login_required decorator, unlike all other partner console endpoints. It is accessible to any unauthenticated user via the URL route /ops/identity/acct-ping-343/.

cwe: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function

extra.message: User input from request.GET['lane'] is passed directly to redirect() without validation. An attacker can craft a URL that redirects users to an external, malicious site (e.g., /ops/after/account-return-lane-093/?lane=https://evil.com).

cwe: CWE-601: URL Redirection to Untrusted Site ('Open Redirect')

extra.message: User-controlled payload (parsed from request.body) is passed directly to workset.update(payload), allowing the attacker to override any key in the dictionary including 'role', 'approved', 'balance', and 'tier', bypassing intended defaults and business logic constraints.

cwe: CWE-915: Improperly Controlled Modification of Dynamically-Determined Object Attributes

extra.message: The Access-Control-Allow-Origin header is set to the value of the request's Origin header, and Access-Control-Allow-Credentials is set to 'true'. This allows any origin to make credentialed cross-origin requests to this endpoint, effectively bypassing the same-origin policy.
X-XSS-Protection is explicitly set to '0' (disabled) and Content-Security-Policy is set to an empty string (removed). This disables browser-level XSS protections for responses from this endpoint.

The random module (not secrets) is used to generate what appears to be a security token ('code'). The random module uses a Mersenne Twister PRNG which is not cryptographically secure; its output can be predicted if the state is known. Security-sensitive tokens should use secrets.choice() instead.

cwe: CWE-338: Use of Cryptographically Weak Pseudo-Random Number Generator (PRNG)

extra.message: ssl._create_unverified_context() is used to create an SSL context that skips certificate verification. This makes the HTTPS connection vulnerable to man-in-the-middle attacks, allowing an attacker to intercept or modify the communication.

Environment variable DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE and internal filesystem path BASE_EXPORT_DIR are exposed in the JSON response. An attacker can use this information to better understand and target the server configuration.

cwe: CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor

extra.message: Exception details including the error message (which contains user input and internal paths) and the exception class name are returned in the JSON response. This reveals internal application structure and filesystem paths to attackers.

cwe: CWE-209: Generation of Error Message Containing Sensitive Information

extra.message: The full request body and Authorization header are logged via logger.warning(). This captures sensitive data such as API keys, credentials, or PII that may be present in the request body or Authorization header into log files.

cwe: CWE-532: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File

extra.message: Hardcoded verification tokens ('north': '4812', 'south': '5930') are embedded directly in source code. Anyone with access to the source code can discover and use these credentials.

Authorization level (elevated vs standard) is determined by the client-controlled 'ops_badge' cookie or 'x-ops-badge' header. An attacker can simply set the cookie or header to 'lead' to gain elevated access, bypassing server-side authorization logic.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: MD5 is used to hash user-supplied input. MD5 is cryptographically broken and vulnerable to collision attacks. It should not be used for any security-relevant purpose.

The Django SECRET_KEY falls back to a hardcoded value 'django-insecure-local-dev-only-change-me' when the environment variable is not set. If deployed without setting SECRET_KEY, session tokens, CSRF tokens, and password reset tokens can be forged by anyone who knows this default.

The default database URL contains hardcoded credentials: 'postgres://crmuser:crmpass@localhost:5432/crm_db'. If DATABASE_URL environment variable is not set, these credentials will be used in production.

DEBUG defaults to True when the environment variable is not set. Running with DEBUG=True in production exposes detailed error pages, stack traces, and application settings to users, which is a critical information disclosure risk.
Imported contact users are assigned the hardcoded default password 'changeme123'. This weak, well-known password is a security risk because it is predictable and users may not change it.

The document filename (from doc.filename()) is interpolated directly into the Content-Disposition header without sanitization. If the filename contains double quotes, newline characters, or other special characters, an attacker could inject arbitrary HTTP headers or break the existing header structure.

cwe: CWE-113: Improper Neutralization of CRLF Sequences in HTTP Headers ('HTTP Response Splitting')

extra.message: The raw API key is included in a Django messages.success() call, which stores the message in the session. This means the raw API key is persisted in the session store, which could be compromised or logged.

cwe: CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor

extra.message: The apikey_revoke view performs a state-changing operation (revoking an API key) without verifying the request method is POST. A GET request from a logged-in user (e.g., via an img tag in a malicious email) would revoke the key, enabling CSRF attacks.

The apikey_rotate view performs a state-changing operation (rotating an API key and generating a new raw key) without verifying the request method is POST. A GET request from a logged-in user would rotate the key, enabling CSRF attacks that could disrupt integrations.
